name: "The Blue Demon" Charlie Williams
caption: A Chicago wrestler with a Batman-styled superhero gimmick, accompanied to the ring by DePaul University's own mascot, who won RLW's first-ever broadcast match.

tenures.source: RLW's own pre-match promo thread for Slamtrack 1's opener (11-13 August 2014) and the Slamtrack 1 broadcast itself (22 August 2014), both served under this wing.

name: FAFNIR
caption: A German heel wrestler billed as "The German Dragon," defeated by Charlie Williams in RLW's first-ever broadcast match.

tenures.source: RLW's own pre-match promo thread for Slamtrack 1's opener and the Slamtrack 1 broadcast (22 August 2014), both served under this wing.

name: "Sci-Fi" Russ Spackler
caption: An Urbana, Illinois wrestler who changes into a different science-fiction-monster persona every few shows and rose to challenge for RLW's own Red Crown Championship at Rush Hour.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 1 broadcast (22 August 2014) through the Rush Hour broadcast (11 January 2015), both served under this wing.

name: the Bullseye Kid
caption: A veteran high-flyer turned rest-hold technician, one half of RLW's own tag team the Haughty Troupe.

tenures.source: RLW's own house-roster listing (served, 8 August 2014) and the Slamtrack 1 broadcast (22 August 2014).

name: Munchy Man
caption: A scarred brawler from Pittsburgh, one half of RLW's own tag team the Haughty Troupe.

tenures.source: RLW's own house-roster listing (served, 8 August 2014) and the Slamtrack 1 broadcast (22 August 2014).

name: Sam Hill
caption: A third-generation wrestler billed the "Redneck Ninja," one of three brothers wrestling together as the House of Hill.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 1 broadcast (22 August 2014) and the Slamtrack 7 preview material naming the House of Hill (1 March 2015), both served under this wing.

name: Simon Hill
caption: One of three brothers wrestling together as the House of Hill, tagging with his brother Sam to defeat the Haughty Troupe on RLW's own debut broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 1 broadcast (22 August 2014), served under this wing.

name: J.J. Hill
caption: One of three brothers wrestling together as the House of Hill, competing solo in RLW's own inaugural Red Crown Tournament.

tenures.source: RLW's own Slamtrack 2 broadcast (11 September 2014, naming the House of Hill's own run-in) and Slamtrack 4's own Red Crown Tournament quarterfinal (29 October 2014), both served under this wing.

name: Raucous
caption: A chaotic, self-destructive high-flyer from Toronto, defeated by BookFace on RLW's own second broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 2 broadcast (11 September 2014), served under this wing.

name: Ukan Jobtamee
caption: A monstrous Russian-styled heel billed the "Bjelkez Butcher," one half of the tag team Winners & Losers with his cousin Ikan Jobtayoo.

tenures.source: RLW's own house-roster listing (served, 6 August 2014) and the Slamtrack 2 broadcast (11 September 2014).

name: The Second Coming
caption: A young, hooded competitor billed "2C," who rose from RLW's own opening-round tournament through a #1 contender elimination match to challenge for the Red Crown Championship.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 2 broadcast (11 September 2014) through the Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), both served under this wing.

BodyCount's own 2015 second-tournament sign-up thread (served under the BodyCount wing, bodycount-2012), in which she signs up for a second Warrior Grand Prix by her own name and call sign ('2C') and states her own federation as Red Line Wrestling

identity.note: A same-named EPW tag team (Bryan Storms and Matt Johansson) shares only the bare dramatic name "Second Coming"; RLW's own character is a solo, unrelated wrestler with no shared roster, moniker, or cross-narration.

notes: Also signed up, in 2015, for a second Warrior Grand Prix run by an unrelated fwrestling.com angle fed, BodyCount (bodycount-2012), under her own name and call sign ('2C') and stating her own federation as Red Line Wrestling -- matching this row's own name and home promotion exactly.

name: "Tacky" Jack Smiley
caption: A public-access-game-show-host gimmick wrestler from Milwaukee, defeated by Kid Koala in RLW's own Red Crown Tournament.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 2 broadcast (11 September 2014) and the Slamtrack 4 broadcast (29 October 2014), both served under this wing.

name: Bryan "The Maniac" Rodgers
caption: An Arizona wrestler forced to hawk his corporate owner's merchandise mid-match, whose Rush Hour bout ended when both men knocked each other out with steel chairs.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 4 broadcast (29 October 2014, naming his RLW debut) and the Rush Hour broadcast (11 January 2015), both served under this wing.

name: "Radical" Roger Stevens
caption: A hard-hitting chop specialist and one-third of the trio J-MAX, formed in Japan under manager Lisa Loeh.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 5 broadcast (7 December 2014) and the Rush Hour broadcast (11 January 2015), both served under this wing.

name: Yoshikazu YAZ
caption: A precision tag-team wrestler from Nagasaki, one-third of the trio J-MAX, formed in Japan under manager Lisa Loeh.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 5 broadcast (7 December 2014) and the Slamtrack 6 broadcast (8 February 2015), both served under this wing.

name: Lisa Loeh
caption: A manager who repackaged Roger Stevens and Yoshikazu YAZ as the trio J-MAX after a falling-out with a rival stable in Japan.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 5 broadcast (7 December 2014) and the Rush Hour broadcast (11 January 2015), both served under this wing.

name: "Wrigleyville's Finest" Johnny Dorn
caption: A perpetually drunk Chicago-bro wrestler who tagged with BookFace as the Hashtag Bros.

tenures.source: RLW's own house-roster listing (served, 15 August 2014), the Rush Hour broadcast (11 January 2015) and the Slamtrack 7 broadcast (1 March 2015), all served under this wing.

name: "The Nightmare" Nic Allen
caption: An intense, apathetic Detroit brawler defeated by El Cabron on RLW's own sixth broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 6 broadcast (8 February 2015), served under this wing.

name: Emevlas Stastias
caption: A heel from Joliet, Illinois billed for her obsession with putting opponents through tables, who upset Skylar Montgomery on RLW's own sixth broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 6 broadcast (8 February 2015) and the Slamtrack 8 broadcast (3 April 2015), both served under this wing.

name: El Habanero
caption: A masked debutant from parts unknown, thrown into a title match against Ivan Dalkichev in his very first RLW appearance.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 7 broadcast (1 March 2015), served under this wing.

name: Steve Jackson
caption: A Chicago wrestler debuting on RLW's own seventh broadcast, disqualified against Normal John Johnson for excessive violence.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 7 broadcast (1 March 2015), served under this wing.

identity.note: A different, ranked wrestler of the same common name is held at a different fwrestling.com federation (WIA, 2003); no document in either record names both, and the name is common enough that no join is asserted.

name: esoteric eric
caption: A depressed, philosophical heel from High Wycombe, England, defeated by The Second Coming on RLW's own seventh broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 7 broadcast (1 March 2015), served under this wing.

name: "Superb" Dick Fury
caption: A sleazy Hollywood wrestler who speaks only in the third person, defeated Go-Go Spectacular on RLW's own eighth broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 8 broadcast (3 April 2015) and the Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), both served under this wing.

name: The Mighty Quinn
caption: An Alaskan wrestler billed for his stoic pride, who defeated Christopher Ryan Eagles by disqualification on RLW's own eighth broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 8 broadcast (3 April 2015) and the Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), both served under this wing.

name: Christopher Ryan Eagles
caption: An English wrestler billed "The Cancer," disqualified for excessive violence against The Mighty Quinn on RLW's own eighth broadcast.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 8 broadcast (3 April 2015), served under this wing.

identity.note: The bare nickname "the Cancer" (one of several akas for this character) is shared with unrelated, already-mutually-distinct held characters at NFW (2000-2001) and CSWA (2000); a name this hobby reuses, per those rows' own existing identity notes. No cross-narration found.

name: Victor Vacio
caption: A mysterious masked luchador who defeated El Cabron on RLW's own eighth broadcast before entering the Slamtrack 10 battle royal.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 8 broadcast (3 April 2015) and the Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), both served under this wing.

name: Hittora
caption: A self-aware Japanese robot wrestler who defeated Emevlas Stastias and later won RLW's own Slamtrack 10 battle royal.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 8 broadcast (3 April 2015) and the Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), both served under this wing.

name: Katie Moicelle
caption: A young former track champion from Crossville, Tennessee, entering RLW's own Slamtrack 10 battle royal in her debut appearance.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), served under this wing.

name: Jessica Cross
caption: A wrestler from Gulf Shores, Alabama by way of Calgary, Alberta, entering RLW's own Slamtrack 10 battle royal in her debut appearance.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), served under this wing.

name: Brad Andrews
caption: A wrestler from a famous wrestling family, competing in RLW's own Slamtrack 10 battle royal in his debut appearance.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), served under this wing.

name: Eric Dane
caption: A veteran wrestler billed the "Only Star," entering RLW's own Slamtrack 10 battle royal on the strength of a long prior career elsewhere.

tenures.source: The Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015), served under this wing.

identity.note: This name recurs across at least three other, unrelated held federations (NFW, CSWA, LOW); RLW's own text claims a prior run in the living DEFIANCE promotion, not in any of those three, and no document anywhere names two of these records together. Filed distinct rather than joined to any of them.

name: The White Hat
caption: A masked, mysterious "gunslinging cowboy from the future-past" who entered RLW's own Slamtrack 10 battle royal.

tenures.source: RLW's own house-roster listing (served) and the Slamtrack 10 broadcast (31 May 2015).

name: Danny Dalton
caption: RLW's own lead commentator, a recent DePaul University communications graduate calling every broadcast this pass could read.

tenures.source: RLW's own backstage-personnel listing and every RLW broadcast served under this wing (22 August 2014 - 31 May 2015).

name: Arin McHenry
caption: RLW's own ring announcer and backstage interviewer, a former DePaul roommate of commentator Danny Dalton.

tenures.source: RLW's own backstage-personnel listing and every RLW broadcast served under this wing (22 August 2014 - 31 May 2015).

name: Greg "Ross" Russell
caption: RLW's own senior referee, a retired lawyer and law professor who calls matches down the middle.

tenures.source: RLW's own backstage-personnel listing and the Slamtrack 1 and Rush Hour broadcasts served under this wing.

name: Jen Glass
caption: RLW's own junior referee, an engineering graduate student and roller derby enthusiast.

tenures.source: RLW's own backstage-personnel listing and multiple RLW broadcasts served under this wing (22 August 2014 - 31 May 2015).
